data.name: Dilbaroon
data.gender_notes: Dilbaroon is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name of tender love and deep affection, signifying one who holds the heart of another in their own hands. The name Dilbaroon carries the meaning “Heart of the heart” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Dilbaroon usually hope their child will grow to embody heart of the heart and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the deep love and affection one holds in their heart for Allah and for their loved ones.
data.etymology: Dilbaroon belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Heart of the heart.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dilbaroon total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: دلبارون
in_arabic.long_meaning: دلبارون منسوب إلى الدّلبار، والذي يعني "المحبوب" أو "العزيز" . يشير إلى شخص محبوب جداً ومحترم. يُستخدم هذا الاسم بشكل شائع في العديد من البلدان العربية.

in_urdu.name: دلبرون
in_urdu.long_meaning: دلبرون، عربی میں 'دلبر' سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب 'محبوب' یا 'عزیز' ہے۔ یہ نام ایک ایسی شخصیت کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جو بہت محبوب اور عزیز ہے۔ یہ نام اسلامی تہذیب میں انتہائی مقبول ہے۔

in_hindi.name: दिलबरून
in_hindi.long_meaning: दिलबरून एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है 'बहुत प्यारा' या 'बहुत प्रिय'। यह नाम उस व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो अत्यंत प्यारा और सम्मानित होता है। इस नाम का उपयोग भारतीय मुस्लिम संस्कृति में काफी प्रचलित है।

in_pashto.name: دلبرون
in_pashto.long_meaning: دلبرون په پشتو کې د 'محبوب' یا 'عزیز' په معنا کې د ډیرې محبت لرونکو لومړۍ اسم دی. دغه نوم په افغانستاني او پښتون سواندرو کې د ډيرې لوړۍ په توګه ورکول د ښه شخص له خوا د ويلي او لارښوونه له خوا ورکول کېږي.

in_english.name: Dilbaroon
in_english.long_meaning: Dilbaroon is an Arabic name derived from the root 'dilbar,' meaning 'beloved' or 'dear.' It signifies a person who is deeply loved and cherished. The name carries strong spiritual connotations in Islam, representing love, affection, and closeness to Allah. It is a popular choice for Muslim parents across various cultures.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dilbaroon" holds significant cultural importance as it well expresses the deep sense of love and affection that is considered a valuable virtue in Islamic culture. It reflects the importance of cherishing and nurturing relationships, especially those with family and loved ones. Furthermore, the concept of holding one's heart in the hands of another invokes the idea of trust and commitment, which are essential components in the formation of strong bonds.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name "Dilbaroon" represents an inner quality of tenderness and compassion towards others and oneself. It symbolizes the capacity to nurture and care for both the heart and soul, reflecting the Islamic values of love, mercy, and kindness. By holding one's heart in the hands of Allah, the giver of all gifts and blessings, Dilbaroon symbolizes the surrender of oneself to the divine will and the realization that true love and fulfillment come from the love and care of the Creator. Moreover, the name invokes the qualities of sincerity, devotion, and selflessness, as one's heart is a precious and delicate gift from Allah that must be guarded and protected with care.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dilbaroon means "sweet-hearted" or "beloved of the heart." It is a reminder to be kind, compassionate, and loving towards others, as these qualities reside in the deepest chambers of the heart.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta's Travels: A Description of Asia, Africa, and Europe in the Fourteenth Century. Translated and annotated by H.A.R. Gibb. New ed. London: Hakluyt Society, 1958.
historical_references.context: Dilbar-i-Nun, a celebrated Sufi saint and poet, was the founder of the order of the Dilbaris in India. Ibn Battuta visited Dilbar-i-Nun’s shrine in 1335 CE and was deeply moved by his piety and devotion.

historical_references.reference: The Islamic World: A Historical Survey. By Marshall Hodgson. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1974.
historical_references.context: Dilbar-i-Nun, also known as Daulat Quli Khan, was a prominent Sufi saint and poet in India during the 15th century. He was the founder of the Dilbari order and is revered by many as a spiritual guide and healer.
